milestone: D3(b) hybrid parry with ownership-aligned QC
code_commit: the commit that adds this file (pushed before the run)
relation_to_d3a: D3(a) (admission_records/director/2026-10-07_d3_preregistration.json, run d3_run1) is FAIL and stays FAIL; its pre-registration and records are unchanged and its ShotSpec still compiles to its archived v1 QC. D3(b) is a NEW experiment with a QC contract aligned to the declared ownership of each component; it does not re-judge D3(a).
question: Can LTX follow the two actors' synchronized choreography closely enough that the system can automatically bind deterministic contact-critical weapon geometry to them and produce one readable, correctly timed parry?

deterministic (Blender, protected): critical weapon continuity (protected layers, all frames)
ownership.rule: QC judges each component by what it owns: actor motion on the generated actors; weapon contact on the authored / delivered weapon layers; raw weapon renders are DIAGNOSTIC (they are replaced)

unchanged_from_d3a: blocked strike and trident parry choreography (engine code unchanged)
compositor (ghost suppression and gain fit unchanged)
changed_from_d3a: QC profile showcase_class_contact_v2 (selected by mace_strike_blocked_v1's qc_profile) instead of showcase_class_preflight_v1
contact_timing (raw mace head, fail) -> raw_mace_contact (same evaluator and params, DIAGNOSTIC)
new fail checks: parry_contact_timing_v2 (attacker hand vs authored grip), defender_reaction_timing (defender rear hand vs authored grip)
new final checks: mace_attached, trident_attached, final_weapon_contact
QC evaluators that raise on a measurement are recorded as failed checks (no executor crash); declared checks without an evaluator still raise
prompt: Create a cinematic shot of a horned Asura attacking an ascetic defender with a heavy mace in an ancient ruined temple at dusk. The defender parries the blow with a trident. Use a low orbit and push-in.
command: uv run onecreations generate "Create a cinematic shot of a horned Asura attacking an ascetic defender with a heavy mace in an ancient ruined temple at dusk. The defender parries the blow with a trident. Use a low orbit and push-in." --run-id d3b_run1

generation.backend: LTX-2.5 22B distilled INT8 ConvRot + Union IC-LoRA (ComfyUI)
generation.prompt: Cinematic dark fantasy film still: an ancient Indian stone temple courtyard at dusk, massive carved sandstone pillars and stone beams, a stepped shrine tower with a glowing lamp-lit doorway, bronze fire braziers, worn cracked flagstones, warm low sunlight from behind with long shadows and soft atmospheric haze. A huge muscular dark-crimson-skinned asura demon with long curved ivory horns, small tusks, glowing amber eyes and a black mane wears a black iron breastplate and heavy layered spiked iron pauldrons tied with leather shoulder straps, a bronze medallion, a leather belt, a dark loincloth with iron tassets, iron knee guards and greaves, and holds a heavy golden spiked mace. Facing him, a lean ash-blue-skinned ascetic with dark matted hair tied in a bun, a white dhoti and a pale shawl holds a steel trident in a guarding stance. Highly detailed skin, metal and stone textures, dramatic cinematic lighting, subtle film grain.

MACE.provenance: P1: heavy_blunt weapon, mace_strike_blocked_v1 estimated peak 1.51 head widths/frame >= 0.7 (local observation, M2-B/768/M3-A/Showcase)

TRIDENT.provenance: P6: TRIDENT takes part in an authored weapon-on-weapon contact

timeline_matches_engine.provenance: D1: compiler and Blender builder compute the same timeline

weapon_bone_projection.provenance: M2-B joint cross-check; Showcase 2.1 px; D3: frames where the weapon is < 90 % visible (ray-cast) are excluded and reported

stationary_root.provenance: M2-B: root and legs never keyed

first_frame_aligned.provenance: first frame rendered from the same scene, camera and frame as the passes (exact by construction)

defender_stationary_root.provenance: D3: the defender's root and legs are never keyed

defender_weapon_axis.provenance: D3: the trident bone lies on the rendered trident (median pixel distance to the projected bone line)

contact_geometry.provenance: D3: the mace head touches the shaft on CONTACT (solved by construction), was clear of it 4 frames before, and no weapon passes through a weapon or a body (vertex distances, ~1 cm resolution)

contact_visible.provenance: D3: both weapons visible at the projected contact

video_valid.provenance: technical validity (decode, count, size, blank or corrupt frames)

subject_framing.provenance: M2 position check (about half a 64-px guide cell)

raw_mace_contact.provenance: D3(b): D3(a)'s contact_timing on the raw mace head, kept as DIAGNOSTIC - the protected mace layer replaces that geometry in every frame

apex_presence.provenance: M2-B apex; calibrated on Showcase v1 run 1

weapon_integrity.provenance: raw fast-weapon failure detector (M2-B / M3-A / Showcase); repaired by the protection policy

defender_framing.provenance: D3: the reacting defender follows the authored pose (the subject_framing rule, plus the contact frame)

trident_integrity.provenance: D3: thin raw weapon detector (masked NCC on the authored trident); evidence for the P6 repair

parry_contact_timing_v2.provenance: D3(b): the generated attacker's hand follows the authored grip from 2 frames before CONTACT to the end of the bind (spatial, trajectory, temporal); thresholds from D2 contact_timing and M3-A attachment

defender_reaction_timing.provenance: D3(b): the generated defender's rear hand follows the authored grip through the raise and the bind

protected_weapon_present.provenance: the repaired weapon survives effects and grade

mace_attached.provenance: D3(b): no severe separation between the delivered protected mace and the generated hand (M3-A 12 px)

trident_attached.provenance: D3(b): no severe separation between the delivered protected trident and the generated hand (12 px)

final_weapon_contact.provenance: D3(b): the delivered protected layers touch on the bind frames (2 px: the 1 cm 3-D tolerance is ~1 px at ~7 m with f = 683 px, plus 1 px of edge antialiasing)

grip_follow (parry_contact_timing_v2, de.max_median_offset_px: 6 = D2 contact_timing max_offset_px (calibrated on Showcase v1 run 1 before D2, frozen in the D2 pre-registration)
grip_follow (parry_contact_timing_v2, de.max_offset_px (settled frames): 12 = M3-A pre-registered attachment limit (grip vs generated hand)
grip_follow (parry_contact_timing_v2, de.settled sub-window: from CONTACT (attacker) / CONTACT-2, the authored block arrival (defender): the per-frame bound skips the fast approach where LTX smears limbs (M2-B); design calibrated on D2's admitted raw only
grip_follow (parry_contact_timing_v2, de.not_from_d3a: D3(a)'s post-hoc ~1 px grip observation was NOT used; the instrument was never run on d3_run1 before this registration

threshold_provenance.attachment (mace_attached, trident_attac: 12 px per settled frame (M3-A attachment limit), lag 0, no appearance (NCC) requirement
threshold_provenance.final_weapon_contact: 2 px between the delivered protected layers on CONTACT..CONTACT+3: the preflight 3-D tolerance 1 cm is ~1 px at ~7 m with f = 683 px, plus 1 px edge antialiasing
threshold_provenance.deterministic 3-D contact: unchanged from D3(a): |gap| <= 0.01 m at CONTACT, >= 0.30 m 4 frames before, min gap >= -0.005 m, body clearance >= 0.10 m

instrument_validation: admission_records/director/2026-10-07_d3b_instrument_validation.json (D2 raw passes; 4-frame-late, 15-px-shifted and time-reversed D2 negatives fail; rehearsal exact)

known_artifacts_not_blocking.orange_streak: the protected mace layer's own authored 90-degree-shutter motion blur at the fastest approach frame (D2 f26, D3(a) post-hoc f28); not a raw ghost, so ghost suppression cannot address it; algorithm unchanged
known_artifacts_not_blocking.trident_brightness: the per-channel gain fit on a thin weapon picks up background (D3(a) post-hoc clipped at 1.6); an owner-relative gain was tested on D2 / rehearsal / D3(a) material and REJECTED (does not reproduce D2's admitted mace gain; unstable on the crimson owner's blue channel); fit unchanged

second_generation_only_if: LTX_GENERATE technical failure (non-zero exit or no output; not the RAM guard)
a post-generation check whose on_fail is 'regenerate' fails (video_valid, output_integrity)
never: regenerate for a failure deterministic repair owns (weapon_integrity, trident_integrity)
regenerate because the result looks weaker
generation_policy.bugs: any code or QC change after the primary generation invalidates AUTONOMY for d3b_run1; the run is recorded as failed and a continuation needs a separately identified run

acceptance.D3b_PASS: AUTONOMY, CONTROL, PIPELINE, FINAL_INTEGRITY and PARRY_READABILITY all PASS
acceptance.D3b_PARTIAL: a final video was delivered by the pipeline but one class is not PASS
acceptance.D3b_FAIL: no final video delivered, or a delivered video fails FINAL_INTEGRITY

PASS: one invocation of the command above produced deliverables/final.mp4 with exit 0
no manual Blender / ComfyUI / compositor / repair / file movement / parameter change after launch
parry_contact_timing_v2 passes (attacker hand / grip interaction timing)
preflight contact_geometry and contact_visible pass (deterministic weapon contact)
CONTROL.FAIL: any of these fails (a 'fail' post-generation check stops the run by itself)

PASS: all 15 stages done in order with keys, times and hashed outputs
REPAIR applied both protected layers (mace_protect P1, trident_protect P6)
QC executed with no evaluator error
final_valid, protected_weapon_present, effects_begin_at_contact, bounded_repair, no_holes pass

visual on the final.mp4 contact sheet (separate from metrics, not a score): guard -> the defender visibly raises the trident -> the mace approaches -> the weapons meet at the authored contact -> the defender braces -> the attacker / mace recoils; no obvious impossible interpenetration; it reads as one block / parry
PARRY_READABILITY.PARTIAL: the contact is on the authored frame but one element does not read
PARRY_READABILITY.FAIL: no visible contact, or a visible impossible interpenetration
